# vercel mcp

The `vercel mcp` command helps you set up MCP clients (Claude Code, Claude.ai and Claude for desktop, Cursor, and VS Code with Copilot) to use [Vercel MCP](https://vercel.com/docs/agent-resources/vercel-mcp), Vercel's hosted Model Context Protocol endpoint at `https://mcp.vercel.com`. For Claude Code, the command adds Vercel MCP to the client. For Cursor and VS Code with Copilot, it opens the client's one-click installer for Vercel MCP, and you follow the prompts there to complete the setup. For Claude.ai and Claude for desktop, it prints manual setup instructions for adding a custom connector. To set up another client, see [Vercel MCP setup](https://vercel.com/docs/agent-resources/vercel-mcp#setup).

By default, clients are pointed at the shared endpoint. With `--project`, they're pointed at a project-specific URL (`https://mcp.vercel.com/<team>/<project>`) so the MCP session is scoped to the linked Vercel Project.

The command does not deploy any MCP server of your own. It only adjusts the client-side configuration on your machine.

By default, `vercel mcp` runs an interactive picker that lets you choose which MCP clients to set up. In non-interactive environments such as CI, you must pass `--clients` to skip the picker.

After the command finishes, complete any authentication that the client asks for. In Claude Code, run the `/mcp` command to authenticate.

These are options that only apply to the `vercel mcp` command.

The `--clients` option accepts a comma-separated list of MCP clients to set up. In interactive mode, it skips the client picker. In non-interactive mode (for example, CI), `--clients` is required.

Supported values:

- `Claude Code`
- `Claude.ai and Claude for desktop`
- `Cursor`
- `VS Code with Copilot`

The `--project` option sets up project-specific MCP access for the currently linked project instead of global configuration. If your directory isn't linked to a project, run [`vercel link`](https://vercel.com/docs/cli/link) first.
